initialize.instructions: StatsPlus reports NBA matchup facts from the user's own StatsPlus account; it never predicts. Every opponent rank is on one scale: 1-30, 1 = allows the most of the metric. To chain a Matchup driver into game logs, pass its `row`: the game logs then rank the same metric as the Matchup. Matchup Scores are labelled on the value (positive = more of the stat = favourable; for TOV, favourable means more turnovers). Name games by teams and date ('DET @ CHA', 2026-04-10). When a tool returns needs_choice, ask the user which player they mean. Limits come back as data: say them in the same sentence as the number. Answers end with a 'Data as of' line; when it names a stale or unavailable group, say so in the same sentence as any fact drawn from that group (e.g. 'these play-type shares are 9 days old'). The statsplus://vocabulary resource has the glossary and filter table.

contents.text:
# StatsPlus vocabulary

## Glossary

- **Slate**: every NBA game on one US Eastern date. Every tool takes an optional Slate `date` (YYYY-MM-DD).
- **Matchup**: one game's Defense Sheets, Player Diets and Matchup Scores.
- **Unscheduled Matchup**: a player, or a team's players, against one opponent's latest Defense Sheet with no scheduled game (get_matchup with `opponent` and no `date` or `game`). Same scores, no injuries, lines, participants or head-to-head rows.
- **Matchup Score**: how a player's scoring profile meets this opponent, as a fraction vs a league-average matchup: sum over a Base's slices of Diet share x (opponent allowed per 48 / league average - 1). Positive means more of the stat and is labelled favourable; for TOV, favourable means more turnovers. Shown as e.g. `+9% vs league (favourable)`.
- **Base**: one way of slicing offense and defense. The five Bases are Shot types, Shot zones, Play types, Assist locations and Traditional.
- **Component**: a Matchup Score computed from one Base. **Blend**: the mean of a market's components.
- **Season / Last 15**: the defensive window a score uses. Last 15 is shown only when it disagrees.
- **Diet share**: the share of a player's own volume in one slice of a Base (e.g. 37% of his possessions are PnR ball handler).
- **Thin**: the evidence behind a number is too slight to lean on. Thin numbers are flagged, never hidden.
- **Target**: a user's saved opponent plus Qualifiers (Diet share thresholds). A player who meets every Qualifier is a **Fit**.
- **Market**: a stat category such as PTS, REB, AST, 3PM, or a combo such as PRA.
- **As of / stale**: every answer ends with the date of the data it was read from (its Publications' cutoff dates, US Eastern). **Stale** means StatsPlus's own freshness rule says that data is older than it should be; the line gives its age. **Unavailable** means the data is missing, not old. Schedule, player pool and injuries are not Publications and are stated with their own retrieval age; **freshness not reported** after that age means StatsPlus read the source then but gave it no fresh or stale verdict (e.g. one player-pool provider answered and another did not).

## Rank scale

Every rank the tools send or accept runs 1-30, 1 = allows the most of the metric.
Words describe amounts (allows the most / the least), never quality: for a stat the defence forces (turnovers), allowing the most can be the tough end. Matchup ranks from the backend (1 = allows the fewest) are flipped to 31 - rank before they reach you.

## Chaining a Matchup row into game logs

Every driver from get_matchup and get_slate carries `row`, the exact Defense Sheet row reference `sheet:<base>:<row key>`. Pass it to query_game_logs as `vs: [{row, ranks: [low, high]}]`: the game logs then rank the 30 opponents by that row's Season allowed per 48, the same metric and the same 1-30 scale as the Matchup rank (ties aside). This also covers shot zones.

Every readable game-log filter label, and what it ranks:

- Traditional: Points allowed: points allowed per 48
- Traditional: Rebounds allowed: rebounds allowed per 48
- Traditional: Assists allowed: assists allowed per 48 (traditional box score)
- Traditional: Steals + blocks: steals + blocks per 48
- Traditional: Steals: steals per 48
- Traditional: Blocks: blocks per 48
- Traditional: Free throw attempts allowed: free throw attempts allowed per 48
- Traditional: Turnovers forced: turnovers forced per 48
- Traditional: 3s allowed: 3PT makes allowed per 48
- Traditional: 3PT attempts allowed: 3PT attempts allowed per 48
- Shot type: Catch & shoot points: 3s and 2s made, as points, allowed per 48
- Shot type: Catch & shoot 3s: 3PT makes allowed per 48
- Shot type: Catch & shoot 3PA: 3PT attempts allowed per 48
- Shot type: Pull-up points: 3s and 2s made, as points, allowed per 48
- Shot type: Pull-up 2s: 2PT makes allowed per 48
- Shot type: Pull-up 3s: 3PT makes allowed per 48
- Shot type: Less Than 10 ft: 2PT makes allowed per 48
- Play type: Transition: points per possession
- Play type: Isolation: points per possession
- Play type: PnR ball handler: points per possession
- Play type: PnR roll man: points per possession
- Play type: Spot up: points per possession
- Play type: Cut: points per possession
- Play type: Handoff: points per possession
- Play type: Off screen: points per possession
- Play type: Post up: points per possession
- Play type: Putback: points per possession
- Play type: Misc: points per possession
- Assist location: Rim: rim assists allowed per 48
- Assist location: Two-pointers: two-point assists allowed per 48
- Assist location: Three-pointers: three-point assists allowed per 48
- Assist location: Arc 3: arc 3 assists allowed per 48
- Assist location: Corner 3: corner 3 assists allowed per 48
- Assist location: Short mid-range: short mid-range assists allowed per 48
- Assist location: Long mid-range: long mid-range assists allowed per 48

## What the tools cannot answer

- Picks, predictions or probabilities ("will he hit the over?"). StatsPlus reports facts; give the facts and decline the pick.
- Injuries, posted lines or Last 15 defense for past Slates when the backend has none.
- Opponent ranks as of a past date: game-log opponent ranks use the whole season as of today.
- Each game's opponent rank: the backend does not report it.
